# Screen demo

The product or result is on a screen, and on-screen action is the spine, with or
without narration. This pack is a sketch assembled from demo inserts in talking-head
edits; measure a reference before leaning on it, then update it.

- Use real capture of the user's product. Ask for recordings or screenshots when a
  claim concerns their data or product.
- Make the cursor, the input and the result readable on a phone: crop or punch in
  toward the action ([geometry](../../references/technical.md#visual-geometry-and-evidence)).
- Shorten by speeding up dead time, never by cutting the result. Show a supplied demo
  for its full length and a supplied table or screenshot whole, long enough to read.
- Label sped-up footage with its playback rate, and update the label when the edit's
  speed changes: a demo shown at 1.15x must not say 1x.
- A surprising result is a natural place for an effect or a 1–2 s reaction cut-in
  (the [skit pack's](../skit/README.md) meme cut).

Quality bar: every step and result is legible at phone size, labels state the true
speed, and nothing the viewer needs to read leaves the screen early.
